question.prompt:
Toothpicks are used to make a grid that is \(60\) toothpicks long and \(32\) toothpicks high. How many toothpicks are used altogether?

[Figure 1](figures/2013_AMC_8_Q22_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Count the horizontal and vertical toothpicks separately. The grid has \(32\) rows of small squares. Including both the bottom and top boundaries requires \(32+1=33\) horizontal lines of toothpicks. Each line contains \(60\), giving
\[
33\times60=1980
\]
horizontal toothpicks.

Similarly, \(60\) columns of squares require \(60+1=61\) vertical lines, including both outside boundaries. Each contains \(32\) toothpicks, giving
\[
61\times32=1952.
\]
Every toothpick is either horizontal or vertical, so these groups include every toothpick exactly once. The total is \(1980+1952=\boxed{3932}\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
solutions.title: Count horizontal and vertical toothpicks

solutions.explanation:
The grid contains \(32\) rows of \(60\) small squares, or \(32\times60=1920\) squares. To count shared sides only once, assign to each square its top toothpick and its right toothpick.

Every horizontal toothpick above the bottom boundary is the top edge of exactly one square. Every vertical toothpick to the right of the left boundary is the right edge of exactly one square. Thus this assignment counts \(2\times1920=3840\) toothpicks without duplication.

The only toothpicks still uncounted are the \(60\) along the bottom boundary and the \(32\) along the left boundary. These are distinct toothpicks, even where the boundaries meet. Therefore the total is
\[
3840+60+32=\boxed{3932},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
solutions.title: Assign two edges to each square
